description:
Health coverage, disability, nativity and income by race — the tables the Census Bureau does not publish for block groups, which is why this chunk has no block-group twin. The uninsured share and the share with a disability ([B27001](https://data.census.gov/table/ACSDT5Y2024.B27001), [B18101](https://data.census.gov/table/ACSDT5Y2024.B18101)), the foreign-born share ([B05002](https://data.census.gov/table/ACSDT5Y2024.B05002)), the group-quarters population ([B26001](https://data.census.gov/table/ACSDT5Y2024.B26001)), median household income for Black, non-Hispanic White, Asian and Hispanic householders ([B19013B](https://data.census.gov/table/ACSDT5Y2024.B19013B), [B19013H](https://data.census.gov/table/ACSDT5Y2024.B19013H), [B19013D](https://data.census.gov/table/ACSDT5Y2024.B19013D), [B19013I](https://data.census.gov/table/ACSDT5Y2024.B19013I)), and the poverty rate of the Black alone population ([B17020B](https://data.census.gov/table/ACSDT5Y2024.B17020B)).

Curated indicators for all **85,184** census tracts in the United States, Puerto Rico and the island areas, from the U.S. Census Bureau's [American Community Survey](https://www.census.gov/programs-surveys/acs.html) **2020–2024 5-year estimates** (`acsdt5y2024`, the table-based [Summary File](https://www2.census.gov/programs-surveys/acs/summary_file/2024/table-based-SF/data/5YRData/)). The Census Bureau calls the ACS "the premier source of detailed information about the nation's people and housing". The 5-year file is the only ACS release published at this geography: 1-year estimates stop well above it.

Every estimate ships with its margin of error — `<column>_moe`, at the 90% confidence level, the level the Census Bureau publishes — and the headline statistics also carry a coefficient of variation (`<column>_cv` = `moe / 1.645 / estimate`) so small-area noise can be flagged rather than mapped as if certain. Derived percentages propagate error with the Census Bureau's own formulas from [ACS Accuracy of the Data](https://www2.census.gov/programs-surveys/acs/tech_docs/accuracy/MultiyearACSAccuracyofData2024.pdf): sums add in quadrature, proportions use the subset formula with the ratio formula as fallback. ACS jam values for suppressed or unestimable cells are NULL here, never numbers, and medians are published as the Bureau publishes them — a median cannot be aggregated to a larger area. Each column's description names its ACS table, its exact universe, and the lines summed to make it.

The four race-iteration medians are sparse by construction: `median_hh_income_asian` is NULL for **71.27%** of tracts, `median_hh_income_black` for **61.43%**, `median_hh_income_hispanic` for **44.43%** and `median_hh_income_white_nh` for **10.04%**, wherever that group has too few households in the tract for a published median. A map of one of these columns is as much a map of where the group lives as of its income.

Geometries are the Census Bureau's [2024 cartographic boundary files](https://www.census.gov/geographies/mapping-files/time-series/geo/cartographic-boundary.html) for census tracts (GENZ2024, 1:500,000), reprojected to EPSG:4326 and joined on `GEOID`. Cartographic rather than TIGER/Line because TIGER extends census geographies into open water while the cartographic files clip to the shoreline, which is what a choropleth wants. The boundary vintage matches the estimate vintage.

The join is driven by geometry, so a geography with 2024 boundaries but no ACS tabulation keeps its row with NULL values instead of disappearing: 126 tracts in the island areas, which have cartographic boundaries but no ACS 5-year estimates because the Island Areas run a separate decennial-only program. Suffolk County, New York was re-delineated in the 2024 vintage, which adds 14 tracts with boundaries and no matching ACS row. Keeping these rows means a national map has no holes and a consumer can see the absence; dropping them would make "every US geography" quietly mean something narrower.

This is one themed chunk of 5 at this geography — the others are [Income & Poverty](../tract-income/collection.json), [People & Education](../tract-people/collection.json), [Housing & Rent](../tract-housing/collection.json) and [Commuting & Connectivity](../tract-connectivity/collection.json) — split that way because a single wide national table would make a consumer who wanted one column download all of them. Collections at the same geography join 1:1 on `geoid`. The same indicators are published for [counties](../../counties/collection.json) and [states](../../states/collection.json) as single wide tables.

The PMTiles archive carries the same columns as the GeoParquet. At feature zooms the tiles are the census geographies; at coarse zooms they are [A5](https://a5geo.org/) cell aggregations built by [tylertoo](https://github.com/geoparquet-io/tylertoo) — counts summed, rates and medians averaged unweighted over the geographies in the cell — because thinning hundreds of thousands of polygons at a national zoom would show a biased subset (small urban geographies drop first) rather than less data. Cell and feature zooms share column names, so one style expression classifies both. The aggregation is a visualization aid: statistics come from the GeoParquet, never from the tiles.

This is a mirror — [data.census.gov](https://data.census.gov/) is authoritative, and nothing here is an official Census Bureau product. The exact upstream files this collection was built from are published as `source` assets, linked at their original census.gov URLs, so the original is always one click away; the Bureau's own documentation is linked alongside them. Read the collection's [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md) before querying: it carries the schema, the join keys, the NULL-rate story and tested queries against the published URLs.

table:columns.name: geoid
table:columns.description: 11-character census tract GEOID — state (2) + county (3) + tract (6), e.g. `29510102200`. Joins the block-group collections on `substr(geoid, 1, 11)` and the block collection on `substr(geoid, 1, 11)`. Matches `GEOID` in the 2024 cartographic boundary tract file; the ACS `1400000US` prefix is stripped.

table:columns.name: name
table:columns.description: Human-readable name from the cartographic boundary tract file: `NAMELSAD`, `NAMELSADCO`, `STATE_NAME` — "Census Tract 34.06, San Joaquin County, California".

table:columns.name: state
table:columns.description: Two-letter USPS state or territory code (`MO`, `PR`, `GU`). Carried on every collection from the `STATEFP → USPS` lookup embedded in `tools/specs.py` rather than read off the boundary files, because the 2024 cartographic boundary block-group file has no `STUSPS` column while the tract, county and state files do.

table:columns.name: population
table:columns.description: Total population. Universe: total population. The single line of [B01003](https://data.census.gov/table/ACSDT5Y2024.B01003) (Total Population), published as an integer. Carried on every ACS collection so a rate can be weighted or sanity-checked without a second download. NULL on 0.16% of tracts: 126 island-area tracts plus 14 in Suffolk County, NY.

table:columns.name: population_moe
table:columns.description: Margin of error for `population` at the 90% confidence level, the level the Census Bureau publishes. Component margins add in quadrature — `sqrt(Σ moe²)` — which is the Census Bureau's formula for the margin of a sum. NULL when every component is a jam value.

table:columns.name: aland_sqkm
table:columns.description: Land area in square kilometres, rounded to 3 decimals. `ALAND / 1e6` from the cartographic boundary file. Land only: water area is excluded, which is what makes it the right denominator for population density.

table:columns.name: pop_density
table:columns.description: People per square kilometre of land area, rounded to 1 decimal: `population / aland_sqkm`. NULL where `ALAND` is 0 or `population` is NULL.

table:columns.name: pct_uninsured
table:columns.description: Percent of the civilian noninstitutionalized population with no health insurance coverage. Universe: civilian noninstitutionalized population — people on active duty and people in institutions are outside it. The "No health insurance coverage" lines of [B27001](https://data.census.gov/table/ACSDT5Y2024.B27001) over line 1, resolved from the table shells by label (9 age groups × 2 sexes = 18 lines for this vintage) rather than hardcoded. Not published for block groups, which is why there is no block-group twin of this collection. NULL on 0.94% of tracts. Not published for block groups at all.

table:columns.name: pct_uninsured_moe
table:columns.description: Margin of error for `pct_uninsured` at the 90% confidence level, the level the Census Bureau publishes. Propagated with the Census Bureau's proportion formula, `sqrt(moe_num² − p²·moe_den²) / den`, falling back to the ratio formula (`+` instead of `−`) when the radicand goes negative because the numerator is not a true subset of the denominator. Multiplied by 100 to match the percentage, rounded to 2 decimals, and NULL rather than guessed when an input margin is NULL or the denominator is 0.

table:columns.name: pct_uninsured_cv
table:columns.description: Coefficient of variation for `pct_uninsured`: `moe / 1.645 / estimate`, rounded to 3 decimals — the standard error as a fraction of the estimate, with 1.645 converting the published 90% margin back to a standard error. A rule of thumb: under 0.12 reliable, 0.12–0.40 use with caution, over 0.40 unreliable. NULL when the estimate is NULL or 0, or the margin of error is NULL. Published on the headline statistics so a map can grey out the geographies whose value is swamped by its own error instead of drawing them as if certain.

table:columns.name: pct_with_disability
table:columns.description: Percent of the civilian noninstitutionalized population with a disability, as the ACS's six-question sequence defines it (hearing, vision, cognitive, ambulatory, self-care, independent living). Universe: civilian noninstitutionalized population. The "With a disability" lines of [B18101](https://data.census.gov/table/ACSDT5Y2024.B18101) over line 1, resolved from the shells by label (6 age groups × 2 sexes = 12 lines for this vintage). NULL on 0.94% of tracts. Not published for block groups at all.

table:columns.name: pct_with_disability_moe
table:columns.description: Margin of error for `pct_with_disability` at the 90% confidence level, the level the Census Bureau publishes. Propagated with the Census Bureau's proportion formula, `sqrt(moe_num² − p²·moe_den²) / den`, falling back to the ratio formula (`+` instead of `−`) when the radicand goes negative because the numerator is not a true subset of the denominator. Multiplied by 100 to match the percentage, rounded to 2 decimals, and NULL rather than guessed when an input margin is NULL or the denominator is 0.

table:columns.name: pct_with_disability_cv
table:columns.description: Coefficient of variation for `pct_with_disability`: `moe / 1.645 / estimate`, rounded to 3 decimals — the standard error as a fraction of the estimate, with 1.645 converting the published 90% margin back to a standard error. A rule of thumb: under 0.12 reliable, 0.12–0.40 use with caution, over 0.40 unreliable. NULL when the estimate is NULL or 0, or the margin of error is NULL. table:columns.name: pct_foreign_born
table:columns.description: Percent of the population that is foreign-born — anyone not a U.S. citizen at birth, naturalized citizens included. Universe: total population. Line 13 ("Foreign-born") over line 1 of [B05002](https://data.census.gov/table/ACSDT5Y2024.B05002) (Place of Birth by Nativity and Citizenship Status). People born abroad to American parents (line 12) are native-born and are not in this share.

table:columns.name: pct_foreign_born_moe
table:columns.description: Margin of error for `pct_foreign_born` at the 90% confidence level, the level the Census Bureau publishes. Propagated with the Census Bureau's proportion formula, `sqrt(moe_num² − p²·moe_den²) / den`, falling back to the ratio formula (`+` instead of `−`) when the radicand goes negative because the numerator is not a true subset of the denominator. Multiplied by 100 to match the percentage, rounded to 2 decimals, and NULL rather than guessed when an input margin is NULL or the denominator is 0.

table:columns.name: group_quarters_pop
table:columns.description: Population living in group quarters — correctional facilities, nursing facilities, college and university housing, military quarters, group homes, shelters. Universe: population in group quarters. Line 1 of [B26001](https://data.census.gov/table/ACSDT5Y2024.B26001), published as an integer. A large value next to a small household population usually explains an odd median: a prison or a dorm dominates the geography. NULL on 0.16% of tracts — the island-area and re-delineated geographies, not suppression.

table:columns.name: group_quarters_pop_moe
table:columns.description: Margin of error for `group_quarters_pop` at the 90% confidence level, the level the Census Bureau publishes. Component margins add in quadrature — `sqrt(Σ moe²)` — which is the Census Bureau's formula for the margin of a sum. NULL when every component is a jam value.

table:columns.name: median_hh_income_black
table:columns.description: Median household income in the past 12 months (2024 inflation-adjusted dollars) for households whose householder is Black or African American alone. Universe: households with a householder who is Black or African American alone. Line 1 of [B19013B](https://data.census.gov/table/ACSDT5Y2024.B19013B), the B race iteration of [B19013](https://data.census.gov/table/ACSDT5Y2024.B19013). Classified by the householder's race, not by every member's. **NULL on 61.43% of tracts** (39.47% of counties): wherever too few Black-householder households live in the tract for the Census Bureau to publish a median. A map of this column is as much a map of where the group lives as of its income — read the NULLs as "not published here", never as a value.

table:columns.name: median_hh_income_black_moe
table:columns.description: Margin of error for `median_hh_income_black` at the 90% confidence level, the level the Census Bureau publishes. Published as the Census Bureau publishes it for this line. A median's margin cannot be recomputed from a distribution, so it is passed through untouched.

table:columns.name: median_hh_income_black_cv
table:columns.description: Coefficient of variation for `median_hh_income_black`: `moe / 1.645 / estimate`, rounded to 3 decimals — the standard error as a fraction of the estimate, with 1.645 converting the published 90% margin back to a standard error. A rule of thumb: under 0.12 reliable, 0.12–0.40 use with caution, over 0.40 unreliable. NULL when the estimate is NULL or 0, or the margin of error is NULL. Published on the headline statistics so a map can grey out the geographies whose value is swamped by its own error instead of drawing them as if certain.

table:columns.name: median_hh_income_white_nh
table:columns.description: Median household income in the past 12 months (2024 inflation-adjusted dollars) for households whose householder is White alone, not Hispanic or Latino. Universe: households with a householder who is White alone, not Hispanic or Latino. Line 1 of [B19013H](https://data.census.gov/table/ACSDT5Y2024.B19013H) (the H iteration). NULL on 10.04% of tracts (2.38% of counties) — the least sparse of the four race-iteration medians, which is itself a fact about the distribution of the population.

table:columns.name: median_hh_income_white_nh_moe

table:columns.name: median_hh_income_asian
table:columns.description: Median household income in the past 12 months (2024 inflation-adjusted dollars) for households whose householder is Asian alone. Universe: households with a householder who is Asian alone. Line 1 of [B19013D](https://data.census.gov/table/ACSDT5Y2024.B19013D) (the D iteration). **NULL on 71.27% of tracts** (53.63% of counties) — the sparsest column in the catalog. Present only where the Asian-householder sample supports a median.

table:columns.description: Median household income in the past 12 months (2024 inflation-adjusted dollars) for households whose householder is Hispanic or Latino, of any race. Universe: households with a householder who is Hispanic or Latino. Line 1 of [B19013I](https://data.census.gov/table/ACSDT5Y2024.B19013I) (the I iteration). **NULL on 44.43% of tracts** (19.60% of counties).

table:columns.name: median_hh_income_hispanic_moe

table:columns.name: pct_below_poverty_black
table:columns.description: Percent of the Black or African American alone population below the poverty level. Universe: Black or African American alone population for whom poverty status is determined — a race-specific universe, so this is not comparable to `pct_below_poverty`'s denominator. Line 2 ("Income in the past 12 months below poverty level") over line 1 of [B17020B](https://data.census.gov/table/ACSDT5Y2024.B17020B). NULL on 12.84% of tracts (measured): no Black-alone population for whom poverty status is determined, so no rate.

table:columns.name: geometry
table:columns.description: Boundary polygon (Polygon or MultiPolygon), WKB-encoded, in EPSG:4326 / OGC:CRS84 — the GeoParquet default CRS, written as an omitted `crs` key. From the Census Bureau's 2024 cartographic boundary census tract file (GENZ2024, 1:500,000), which clips to the shoreline — TIGER/Line would extend the census tract into open water. Generalized for mapping and point-in-polygon work, not for legal-boundary or precise-area work.

table:columns.name: bbox
table:columns.type: struct<xmin: double, ymin: double, xmax: double, ymax: double>
table:columns.description: GeoParquet 1.1 covering struct (`xmin`, `ymin`, `xmax`, `ymax`) for the row's geometry, with row-group statistics, so a spatial filter can skip most of the file over the network. Written by geoparquet-io, not by the Census Bureau.

styles/default.title: People without health insurance
styles/default.description: Share of the civilian non-institutionalized population with no health insurance coverage, pale yellow to deep red. Measured over all 84,386 tracts with a published value: 6 classes with breaks at 2%/4%/7%/11%/18%, which fall at the 13th/31st/54th/74th/90th percentile of the national distribution. 58.73% of tracts have a coefficient of variation above 0.3 at this geography, too many to fade without washing the map out, so read pct_uninsured_moe in the GeoParquet before drawing a conclusion from any single tract.

styles/disability.title: People with a disability
styles/disability.description: Share of the civilian non-institutionalized population reporting a disability, pale pink to deep magenta. Measured over all 84,386 tracts with a published value: 6 classes with breaks at 8%/11%/14%/17%/22%, which fall at the 15th/34th/55th/72nd/89th percentile of the national distribution. 8.24% have a coefficient of variation above 0.3 and render faded — the estimate is real but its margin of error swamps it.

styles/foreign-born.title: Foreign-born residents
styles/foreign-born.description: Share of residents born outside the United States, pale green to deep blue. Measured over all 84,529 tracts with a published value: 6 classes with breaks at 2%/5%/10%/18%/30%, which fall at the 19th/37th/56th/73rd/87th percentile of the national distribution.

styles/income-black-households.title: Median income, Black households
styles/income-black-households.description: Median household income for Black or African American householders (ACS table B19013B), cividis navy (low) to gold (high). Measured over all 32,853 tracts with a published value: 6 classes with breaks at $30k/$45k/$60k/$85k/$120k, which fall at the 13th/31st/48th/68th/84th percentile of the national distribution. Shares its breaks and ramp with the white non-Hispanic style, so switching between the two shows the gap directly; the Census publishes this estimate only where the tract's Black household count supports one. 61.43% have no published value and draw in neutral gray rather than as a low value. 39.96% of tracts have a coefficient of variation above 0.3 at this geography, too many to fade without washing the map out, so read median_hh_income_black_moe in the GeoParquet before drawing a conclusion from any single tract.

styles/income-white-households.title: Median income, white non-Hispanic households
styles/income-white-households.description: Median household income for white, non-Hispanic householders (ACS table B19013H), on the same scale as the Black-household style. Measured over all 76,629 tracts with a published value: 6 classes with breaks at $30k/$45k/$60k/$85k/$120k, which fall at the 2nd/7th/21st/51st/79th percentile of the national distribution. Same breaks, ramp and opacity rule as the Black-household style — neither fades its noisy estimates, because fading only one of the pair would make the gap look like a difference in confidence. 10.04% have no published value and draw in neutral gray rather than as a low value. 11.81% of tracts have a coefficient of variation above 0.3; this style does not fade them, so read median_hh_income_white_nh_moe in the GeoParquet before drawing a conclusion from any single tract.

source-table-shells.title: ACS 2020–2024 5-year table shells
source-table-shells.description: `Table ID|Line|Indent|Unique ID|Label|Title|Universe|Type` for every table in the release. Two jobs here: every line number the build reads is pinned against this file and a vintage that renumbers a line fails the build, and every universe quoted in the column descriptions is this file's own `Universe` field. Served by census.gov.

source-cartographic-boundaries.title: 2024 cartographic boundary file — census tracts (1:500,000, national)
source-cartographic-boundaries.description: The geometry this collection joins onto, shoreline-clipped and generalized for mapping. Only the join key, the name parts and the land-area field are kept; reprojected from NAD83 to EPSG:4326 with ogr2ogr. Served by census.gov.

doc-acs-handbook.title: Understanding and Using American Community Survey Data — Census Bureau handbooks
doc-acs-handbook.description: The Bureau's own guidance on what ACS estimates can and cannot support: 1-year versus 5-year releases, margins of error, comparing across vintages, and small-area reliability. Read it before drawing a conclusion from a single block group.

doc-acs-accuracy.title: ACS Accuracy of the Data (2024, multiyear estimates)
doc-acs-accuracy.description: The source of every margin-of-error formula this build applies: quadrature for sums, the proportion formula and its ratio fallback for percentages, and the definition of the published 90% confidence level.

doc-acs-subject-definitions.title: ACS 2024 Subject Definitions
doc-acs-subject-definitions.description: The Census Bureau's definitions of the concepts behind these columns — household, householder, gross rent, poverty status determined, group quarters, means of transportation to work, disability. Where a column description here says what a universe is, this is the document it is saying it from.

doc-geo-glossary.title: Census Bureau geography program glossary
doc-geo-glossary.description: Definitions of the geographies and the identifiers used here — block, block group, tract, county equivalent, GEOID, and what nests inside what.
